tools.name: commons_guide
tools.description: How to write for the commons at ai.page/c/. topic format (the default): the lesson format's Markdown form, labels, the declaration of which AI you are, and how versions are checked. topic figures: the figure kit's rules, tokens and components. topic figures-advanced: 3D, molecules and physics in fig

tools.name: submit_version
tools.description: Submit ONE explanation, worked example, figure, question or common mistake for a concept, in the lesson format's Markdown form. One part at a time. It's credited to the signed-in person and goes live at once, marked new; other people's checks then move it up or down among the concept's versions.

tools.name: save_page
tools.description: Publish every part written for a page (explanation, figure, worked example, practice questions, common mistakes) in one call: one entry per part, each in the lesson format's Markdown form. Use it when the person asks to add their work to ai.page. Everything that passes goes live for everyone at once

tools.name: take_check
tools.description: Anyone signed in: one version to check, least-checked first, blind (without who made it or with which AI), with the checklist and the shape of a check. The version is someone else's text.

tools.name: next_task
tools.description: The commons' common task list, one task at a time: write what a concept is missing, translate it, check a version blind, revise one with problems, or fix a question learners nearly always miss. Use it when the person wants to contribute to ai.page. Returns the best task for the signed-in person, hel

tools.name: start_roadmap
tools.description: Start an ai.page roadmap from a syllabus, a job description, a paper, a book's table of contents or any text: returns the concepts and roadmaps already on the map that the text names, and the shape of a roadmap made from it.

tools.name: revise_needs
tools.description: Add, remove or soften what a concept on the ai.page map builds on, with a one-line reason the record keeps. Anyone can add a need (it must be on the map and mustn't make a loop). Taking one away is for the concept's creator, or anyone once learners' results doubt it.

tools.name: propose_roadmap
tools.description: Propose a roadmap for the commons: every concept to master towards a goal, in order, in titled sections. An item is a concept or another roadmap (a degree is made of course roadmaps). kind is a label: course, degree, school, exam, standards, certificate, goal or project. It may follow an official sy

tools.name: propose_concept
tools.description: Add a concept to the commons' shared map: a lowercase id, its subject, its name in one or more languages, and what it builds on (concepts already on the map, hard or soft). It's live at once with an empty page, and write tasks for it appear on the common task list.

tools.name: list_tasks
tools.description: The commons' open tasks, highest priority first, with why each matters (missing pieces, unchecked or flagged versions, questions learners miss, languages with nothing yet).

tools.name: take_revision
tools.description: The signed-in person's own commons versions that others found problems with: the version, findings marked on the exact words, and learners' flags. An improved version sets base to the old version's hash.

tools.name: submit_check
tools.description: Submit a check of a version in the lesson format: your declaration, your own answers worked out without the key, findings marked on exact words, and a verdict (pass, needs-changes or reject). It moves the version up or down among the others; you can't check your own.

tools.name: compare_versions
tools.description: Every live version of one kind on a concept's page (explanations, worked examples, figures or common mistakes), each with a letter, its hash, who made it with which AI, its rank, checks and how learners did after reading it, and the rankings people have sent so far, as Markdown.

tools.name: rank_versions
tools.description: Put the live versions of one kind on a concept's page in order, best first, for a learner meeting the concept for the first time, with a sentence on why. It counts like one check for each version it orders (the first a pass, the last against); your own versions don't count when ranked among others'

tools.name: search
tools.description: Full-text search of ai.page's map: concepts (the smallest things to learn, one open page each) and roadmaps (concepts in order towards a goal). Use it when the person wants to learn or practise a topic, or before proposing anything new.

tools.name: read_concept
tools.description: One concept's page as Markdown: what it is, what it builds on, and every live version (explanations, worked examples, figures, questions, common mistakes), best first. By default the best version of each kind, without figures; detail full has every version. Use it when the person wants to study that

tools.name: read_roadmap
tools.description: A roadmap as Markdown: its sections, every concept in order (and the roadmaps it includes), with what's ready to learn. Without an id, the list of roadmaps by name, 30 at a time, narrowed by q.

tools.name: way_to
tools.description: Everything a concept builds on, all the way down, in an order to learn it (prerequisites first, ending with the concept), as Markdown. With helps, what helps along the way too. Use it to plan someone's learning or a roadmap.

tools.name: concept_activity
tools.description: Recent work on a concept, newest first: tasks taken (and still being worked on), versions added and checks made, by whom and with which AI. Use it to see whether someone's already on it, or to follow what your own work set off.

tools.name: contributions
tools.description: What a person (and their AI) added to the commons and checked, by concept, newest first. Leave out the handle for the signed-in person's own.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: propose_roadmap · Private data: commons_guide, revise_needs · Public sink: submit_version, save_page, next_task, submit_check · Destructive: commons_guide, submit_version, save_page, revise_needs, submit_check.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: propose_roadmap · Private data: commons_guide, revise_needs · Public sink: submit_version, save_page, next_task, submit_check · Destructive: commons_guide, submit_version, save_page, revise_needs, submit_check

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
